title: TIC monthly release (March 2027 data), 4:00 p.m. ET — not the pure control it was proposed as: it is note (d)'s own May slot, and the FOMC minutes land on its scored session
source: TSY: home.treasury.gov/data/treasury-international-capital-tic-system/release-dates-of-tic-data, re-fetched direct 2026-09-09 by this event's own initial-research session (plain curl, HTTP 200, 111,194 bytes) and re-parsed column by column rather than inherited from the proposal. The 2027 May row reads '18' in the Monthly column with BOTH quarterly columns and BOTH annual columns EMPTY — a single-cut monthly release — under the page header 'All data releases occur at 4 p.m. Washington, D.C. time'. Reference month March 2027 by the page's own 'end of month before last' rule, independently corroborated by the publisher's own archive, which labels the 2026-05-18 release 'TIC Data for March 2026'. MECHANICAL CORROBORATION, and it is the strongest offset record in this series: the 11th business day of May 2027 is 2027-05-17 (Monday), putting the published 2027-05-18 at +1 business day, inside the page's stated window. Treasury's own release-date archive gives twenty-three published May dates 2004-2026, of which TWENTY-ONE CONSECUTIVE (2004 through 2024) land on the 11th business day EXACTLY; the only non-zero offsets in the whole record are 2025 (+1) and 2026 (+3). May 2027's only 5 U.S.C. 6103 federal holiday is Memorial Day 2027-05-31, which falls after the 11th business day, so this date discriminates nothing between the holiday-aware and holiday-blind readings of the rule — stated rather than smoothed. Promoted estimate -> confirmed by this session, which is the event's own and therefore is not bound by the proposer's no-self-confirm limit; the confirmation covers THE PUBLISHED SCHEDULE AND NOTHING ELSE. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: CANONICAL FILE written by this event's own never-assessed initial research (2026-09-09) after reading the one prior proposal, proposals/tic-monthly-2027-05-18.from-tic-monthly-2027-04-15.json, which it now shadows. THE PROPOSAL PICKED A REAL SLOT AND GAVE IT TWO WRONG JOBS. (1) 'A PURE ORDINARY EDITION' IS THE ONE THING A MAY EDITION IS NOT. Treasury's note (d), verbatim from the page this session fetched: 'Before September 2011, revised data back to the previous June was usually released in March to include preliminary data from the annual survey... THE MAY RELEASE usually included the final results from that survey.' The only evidence anyone in this series has that a survey benchmark still reaches the monthly data is FT-tic-monthly-2027-01-19-3's three excluded Feb/Mar outliers — and the mechanism offered for them is the PRELIMINARY survey's feed. May is that mechanism's other half: 2027-05-18 stands 18 days after the final survey (2027-04-30). Calling it a pure control assumes the answer to the question it was proposed to test. (2) THE CORRIDOR IS NOT CLEAN — FIVE tracked events sit within +/-5 days against April's two, and fomc-minutes-2027-05-19 lands ON the scored session (14:00 ET, estimate, from the Fed's own re-measured three-week rule). The proposal measured the distance to the next FOMC DECISION (+22 days) and to expirations, and never checked minutes. So NO TIC-KEYED TAPE TEST IS REGISTERED HERE: April restored one, May refuses again, on attribution rather than on expected noise — the collision class is measured and QUIET (11 of 143 era releases already scored on a minutes day: mean 2.73bp, max 7.0bp). Two further measured reasons a May tape test would be the wrong one: the May edition bucket is the NOISIEST plain month (4.083bp, n=12, sd 3.40, max 10.0 — the only Feb/May/Aug/Nov bucket above the 3.993bp all-session baseline), and the twelve-month bucket table this session built shows NO revision-versus-ordinary ordering at all (noisiest is March at 4.667bp, a quarterly-cut month; quietest is August at 2.583bp, a plain one). Impact LOW and symbols empty on the standing grounds: 16:00 ET publication after the equity cash close, six-week-stale data, and no house playbook is macro-keyed. Nothing here licenses an entry.
